clips.name: Tight bathroom-counter photograph: woman stirring fiber into a clear water glass beside recognizable magnesium and laxative packages. Modest cool morning light.

Closer cross-section of the descending colon with dry formed stool visible and room around it. The view should immediately read as slow bowel transit, not a person waiting in a bathroom. Glossy pink realistic tissue, deep navy background, no sealed obstruction or huge pile.

Establish the overlooked upstream/downstream relationship in one close full-frame medical CGI view: connected stomach above, small bowel center, colon framing the lower area. The stomach receives a restrained amber locator while the colon remains visible below; no face or everyday scene.
Whole digestive tract; amber highlight stays on the anatomically correct stomach. Slow, subtle movement rather than a frozen or sealed organ.

Close three-quarter cutaway of the descending and sigmoid colon, showing a small number of firm dry stool segments with an open route between and around them. This is an illustration of constipation and delayed transit. Glossy pink folded tissue on deep charcoal navy, no numbers or clock needed.
Four quick object reveals on the counter, one per named remedy. Use real package references; allow internal picture changes on each product name.
Torso diagram: camera travels down the continuous digestive tract and highlights the colon. Keep the stomach visible in the same diagram.
Closer view of the colon in the same diagram. A simple editor-set COLON label lands beside it; no empty-tube claim.
Hard cut back to the upper torso. Highlight the stomach at the exact word stomach; the entire tract remains connected.
Stomach cross-section shows a modest meal and gradual mixing; no solid brick, stool, complete obstruction, or food packed into the esophagus.

Medical CGI composition showing a coherent stomach and colon connected by small bowel, paired with a small simple analog clock outside the anatomy at the edge. Stomach contains a modest meal while colon is visible below. The clock is a time metaphor for temporary relief, not a measured treatment comparison. No day count or charts, no face.

Tight anatomical stomach cutaway: modest partly digested meal with visible soft plant-fiber strands dispersed among the food and fluid. Show the feeling of fullness through contents occupying part of the stomach, not excessive swelling, a solid blockage or feces in the stomach. Organ fills the portrait frame in glossy salmon-pink educational CGI.

Side-view educational cutaway of the upper stomach and connected esophagus rising toward the cropped throat, with a few translucent gas bubbles above the modest meal and beginning to enter the esophagus. Illustrate the upward route of a burp; no human face, cartoon green cloud or rotten eggs inside the body.

Reassuring intact digestive-system CGI, continuous healthy-looking pink stomach, small bowel and colon within a faint transparent torso outline. Neutral illumination without damaged organs, warning marks or cure-like glow. Close vertical crop with no face; anatomy, not an emotional portrait.
Her hand sets the correctly referenced medication pen beside its box. Do not show injection technique or throw medication away.
One full-frame anatomy map. Two editor-set callouts read STOMACH / UPSTREAM and COLON / DOWNSTREAM. Alternate emphasis between them.
Stay on the neutral stomach map. A soft highlight introduces the proposed movement-support job. No switch flipping, nerve repair, or restart demonstration.
Camera moves down the same connected tract; a second quiet highlight joins the first. Keep the diagram visually continuous.
Three clean numbered ingredient spaces fill the frame. Show 1, 2, 3; no product bottle or Motilli mark yet.
Macro of washed celery stalks and a small glass of green juice on cream stone. Editor-set APIGENIN / FROM CELERY label; first checklist dot fills.
Neutral illustrative stomach with an external wave line indicating the intended job. No causal before/after animation showing celery restarting contractions.

Conceptual microscopic-style illustration of soluble dietary fiber dispersed in clear water: a few separate fine translucent pale strands suspended among clear blue water droplets, freely dispersed rather than a gel mass. Deep navy backdrop, dimensional macro photography-like CGI, coherent sparse composition. This is a material concept, not an exact molecular structure; no atoms with fake bonds, chemical formula, numbered particles, powder bowl or person.
Restrained diagram of water and stool inside the colon; label this an illustrative concept. Do not show FOS behaving as a proven gel-forming osmotic agent.

Macro educational cutaway looking along an open section of intestine with a small amount of clear fluid and sparse fine dispersed fiber strands. Keep plenty of open lumen visible and smooth glossy pink wall folds; no giant mass, brick, pile, bottle, comparative chart or zero-bulk claim. This illustrates material dispersed in fluid, rather than product packaging.
Deep-green chlorophyllin ingredient material in a laboratory-style glass dish, editor-set CHLOROPHYLLIN label; third checklist dot fills. No fabricated molecular binding.

Close side cutaway of the stomach-esophagus junction, with a few translucent gas bubbles clustered above a modest meal and travelling toward the lower esophagus. Focus on the internal origin and route of burps. A tiny neutral mint lozenge may sit outside the anatomical illustration at the lower edge as an odor-masking cue, never inside the organ. No person, invented chemical binding, treatment particles or mint packet.
FIRST MOTILLI REVEAL: the verified current bottle enters between the three ingredient dishes. Label faces the lens and remains readable.
Macro of exactly two dark-green heart-shaped gummies beside the bottle. Preserve true gummy shape and finish from the reference.

Anonymous adult female torso medical illustration, cropped shoulders to hips without face or nudity, its outer surface translucent pearlescent and the connected digestive organs visible inside. Keep a modest neutral medical silhouette and a restrained locator at the stomach. Same glossy pink organs and dark slate scientific aesthetic.

Object-only view through the doorway of the same ordinary beige bathroom, with a closed toilet lid, tiled floor and door slightly open. No person, face, reflection, body, text or product. Tight purposeful composition that directly depicts a trip to the bathroom, not another smiling portrait.

Close longitudinal educational cutaway of a short segment of colon with a modest soft formed stool segment and a visibly open passage, showing the physical meaning of regular movement. Pink realistic folds and subtle muscular contours, navy background. Normal digestive movement illustration only, no before/after, drug, product particles, clock or guarantee.
Morning light on the same woman sitting up in bed; cut to a neutral bathroom-door detail. Editor label: IMAGINE YOUR MORNING.
She puts on a light cardigan over her usual tee and takes her bag. No altered waist size, flatter-stomach comparison or jeans transformation.
Over-shoulder view of her choosing a time for coffee with a friend; hard cut to her picking up keys. Any phone text is added in the editor, not generated.
Eye-level exterior portrait just outside the same home; natural small smile, relaxed shoulders and warm daylight.

Object-only close-up of the same existing capped blue medication pen lying beside its plain carton on the bathroom counter, with a softly out-of-focus ordinary weekly planner in the background. No person or visible hand. Keep the pen cap on, preserve its identity, no dose numbers, scale, body comparison or added readable text. Direct visual of continuing the established shot routine.
Verified current bottle and exactly two dark-green heart-shaped gummies on cream stone. Editor-set brand, 90-DAY MONEY-BACK GUARANTEE and SHOP MOTILLI. Add a two-second silent tail.

markers.body: On a GLP-1, the harder you push your colon
with laxatives and fiber, the more stuck you can feel.
Here’s the trap no one explains.
Your GLP-1 slows your stomach down.
So when you haven’t gone in days,
you reach for MiraLAX, magnesium, stool softeners, or more fiber.
Those products work downstream. They target the colon—
the end of your digestive system.
But if the slowdown begins higher up in your stomach,
food is still sitting at the beginning.
That’s why the relief may last a day,
the fiber can make you feel even fuller,
and those rotten-egg burps keep coming back.
It’s not that your body is broken.
And it doesn’t mean you have to quit your shot.
You’ve been trying to solve an upstream slowdown with downstream tools.
What you need is something designed to wake your stomach back up
while supporting everything below it.
And to do that, you need three specific things.
First, apigenin—a plant compound concentrated from celery juice—
to support your stomach’s natural wave-like movement.
Second, a low-viscosity soluble fiber
that holds water in the stool
without becoming another heavy bulk load.
And third, chlorophyllin to neutralize the sulfur compounds
behind those burps instead of merely covering the smell.
That’s why Motilli combines all three
in two heart-shaped gummies made specifically for people on GLP-1s.
For women on a GLP-1,
the goal isn’t just another trip to the bathroom.
It’s feeling regular again—and getting on with your day.
Imagine waking up, going comfortably,
and getting dressed without wondering how long it’s been.
Making plans without your stomach being the first thing you think about.
You want to feel like yourself again,
without giving up the progress you’ve worked for.
